challenge.name: The Locked Shadow
challenge.description: A supplier contract for the next promotion week is already signed, and the team cannot deploy the new model without a shadow run to verify it. #reliability_ruth# demands a fully automated and governed shadow environment to protect the live forecast, while #automation_alex# insists on keeping it manual to avoid breaking the current pipeline stability.

output.content: We are locking the shadow environment as the top priority for the next sprint. I am willing to accept leaving the model serving endpoint without formal governance review for the time being. This trade off allows us to focus all validation effort on verifying the new allocation logic against the signed supplier contract. We need the shadow run to prove reliability before we touch the live pipeline. The serving endpoint can remain in its current manual state while we build the automated verification layer. This compromise ensures we do not break the live forecast while we secure the new deployment path. The lack of governance on the serving side is a temporary concession to get the shadow infrastructure running safely.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to accept leaving the model serving endpoint without formal governance review to prioritize the shadow environment, which fits the definition of stating something they would give up or accept losing.
